HIS   T BAIL   APPLICATION   HAVING   COME   UP   FOR  ADMISSION  ON  15.02.2024, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING: 
 B.A.NO.624 OF 2024   2   
 RDER O  Dated this the 15 th  day of February, 2024  This  is an application for anticipatory bail under  Section 438  of  Cr.P.C. 
filed  by  accused  Nos.1  and  2  in  crime  No.75  of  2 0 2 4   o f   C h a l a k u d y   P o l i c e   S t a t i o n , 

Thrissur,
registered under Sections 467,
406 and 420 r/w  Section 34 of IPC.

2. 
The  prosecution  allegation  is  that, 
petitioners 1  and  2, 
forging  the signature  of  the  defacto complainant, 
obtained  loan  of  Rs.2,00,000/-
 f r o m   P a r i y a r a m   M e k h a l a   V a n i t h a  Co-operative Society,
where the 1st accused is a  Board  Member  and  the 2nd  accused  is  an  Attender, 
and  thus they cheated the defacto complainant. 
3.

Heard  learned  counsel  for  the  petitioners  and  learned Public Prosecutor. 
4.

Learned
Public  Prosecutor  opposed  the  bail  application.

5. 
Learned counsel  for  the  petitioners  would B.A.NO.624 OF 2024   3   
submit  that the  defacto  complainant, 
on  the  request  made  by  the  petitioners,

agreed  to  avail  a  loan  in  her  name, 
and  the  amount  was  given to  the  petitioners.

Later,
the petitioners cleared that liability.
So they never  cheated  the  defacto  complainant.

They  are  ready  to abide by any conditions imposed by this Court. 
6. 
Learned  Public  Prosecutor, 
on instructions, 
submitted  that  the  2nd petitioner forged the documents,

and availed loan from the Co-operative Bank,
without the  knowledge  of the  defacto  complainant.
Learned  Public  Prosecutor  further  submitted  that the  loan  amount  availed  by  the  petitioners  in  the  name  of  the defacto  complainant  was  already  paid  off  by  the  petitioners.

Since  the forgery  alleged  is  to  be  investigated  by  collecting  further  information and  documents  available  with  the  petitioners, 
their  presence  is  required as  submitted  by  learned  Public  Prosecutor.

Moreover, 
the B.A.NO.624 OF 2024   4   
petitioners  had  availed  loans  in  the  name  of  about  10 persons, 
by  forging  their  signatures, 
and  that  fact  also  has to be investigated properly.

7. 
Admittedly, 
the  petitioners  paid  off  the  loan amount  availed  in  the  name  of  the  defacto complainant. 
Whether  the defacto  complainant  had  agreed  for  taking  that  loan  or  it  was  taken without  her  knowledge  by  forging  her  signature  etc. 
is  to  be  found o u t  a f t e r  c o n d u c t i n g d e t a i l e d i n v e s t i g a t i o n .

8 . 

Considering the fact that the petitioners paid off  the  loan  amount a v a i l e d  i n  t h e  n a m e  o f  t h e  d e f a c t o  complainant,
and both petitioners are ladies,
and the 1st  petitioner  is  a senior  citizen, 
this  Court  is  inclined  to  allow this bail application on the following terms:

(i) 
The  petitioners  shall  surrender  before  the  Investigating Officer  on  or  before  21.02.2024, 
and  shall  subject  themselves  for interrogation.

The  Investigating B.A.NO.624 OF 2024   5   
Officer  can  collect all  material/evidence  relevant  for  the  purpose of investigation from the petitioners.

(ii) 
In  the  event  of  arrest, 
the  petitioners  shall  be  released  on  bail Thressiamma vs State Of Kerala on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27288645/
2 on  executing  bond  for  Rs.1,00,000/-(Rupees  One  Lakh  only) 
with  two solvent  sureties  each  for  the  like  sum  to  the  satisfaction  of  the arresting officer; 
(iii) 
Thereafter, 
the  petitioners  shall  appear  before  the Investigating  Officer on alternate Saturdays starting from

and  11.00  a.m., 
for  a  period  of  three  months or  till  the  final  report  is  filed, 
whichever is earlier. 
(iv)

The petitioners shall not influence or intimidate the  witnesses or tamper with the investigation. 
(v) 
The  petitioners shall not commit any offence while  on bail. 
(vi)
In case of violation of any of the aforesaid conditions,
B .

the jurisdictional Court is empowered to cancel their bail, 
in accordance with law.
